extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It contains 6,141 examples drawn from 31 source datasets, including 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was assembled by collecting 9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets, then filtering examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning using heuristic rules (e.g., numeric answers or quantity words) and manually labeling selected examples. Three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were also created and manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields, followed by review and majority voting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations; the paper notes that annotations were sourced from original data providers and that some examples lack annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multimodal datasets in math-targeted QA and VQA settings, plus newly sourced puzzle test figures, functional plots, and academic paper figures from online learning platforms and papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Existing source datasets span various years; the newly sourced PaperQA examples were taken from papers released in August 2023. Human evaluation for GPT-4V was conducted from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023, and Multimodal Bard evaluation from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Source datasets were capped at up to 400 examples each to balance representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic filtering selected likely math-related examples, followed by manual labeling and majority voting. For the final benchmark, examples were split into testmini and test, with testmini sampled to closely match the full distribution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic filtration of candidate VQA examples using heuristic rules based on numeric answers or quantity words; manual review to determine whether examples involved mathematical reasoning; majority voting to finalize labels; quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and reasoning skills. Newly collected datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. For mathematical reasoning labels, three reviewers independently annotated each dataset and disagreements were resolved through discussion.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: An annotation tool with a GUI was used; human performance and assessment tasks were conducted on Amazon Mechanical Turk; GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For mathematical reasoning problem labeling, the paper reports a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 among three annotators. For the newly collected questions, 99.2% inter-annotation consistency was reported, with only 6 disagreements among 736 questions, resolved by discussion. For automatic reasoning-type annotation, 94.1% exact set agreement and 98.79% individual label agreement were reported against human annotations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three reviewers annotated each newly collected dataset item; for mathematical reasoning labeling, three annotators were used. For human performance evaluation, each question was assigned to five annotators.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for dataset annotation; human performance annotators on AMT were required to have a high school diploma or higher, a history of more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor; EasyOCR was used to detect OCR text; Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions; an annotation GUI was used for manual labeling.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is maintained online with an evaluation platform. The test set answer labels will not be publicly released to prevent contamination. The authors state they will maintain the dataset, refine potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolve the leaderboard as new models appear.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language, grade level, and educational attainment of annotators were collected; the benchmark also includes non-English questions (including Chinese and Persian). Human evaluation annotators were screened by education level.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of general-purpose AI agents for mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, including educational, analytical, theorem-proving, and scientific discovery applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that source datasets are heterogeneous and that annotations lack a unified format. It also reports that the dataset includes 6.57% non-English questions and that source datasets were capped at 400 examples each, which may affect representation. The benchmark is balanced across tasks and sources, but coverage gaps remain.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may have gaps in coverage of certain mathematical problems and visual contexts. Its focus on visual mathematical reasoning makes collection labor-intensive, and scalability/generalizability to other domains remains a concern. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and the authors note potential data noise and heterogeneous annotation formats. The test set labels are withheld, so the benchmark is not fully open for direct answer access.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for testing, validation, and model development on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. testmini is intended for model development validation or limited-compute settings, while test is for standard evaluation. The benchmark is also used for comparing LLMs and LMMs under zero-shot, few-shot, CoT, PoT, and tool-augmented settings.
